fatal_errors: The proposed 850/950 °C two-stage treatment replaces the target SPS optimum at 1000 °C and never tests a 1000 °C sample.
The local-chemical-order and embrittlement mechanism is transferred from unrelated HEA systems without evidence that it occurs in the proposed Mg-V-Nb or Mg-Mo-Nb alloys.
The proposed protective oxides include Cr2O3 and CrTaO4 even though Cr and Ta are absent from the suggested compositions; formation of a protective, self-healing MgO/NbO2 layer is also unsupported.
Corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl is omitted from the falsification experiment, so the claimed barrier performance against chloride penetration cannot be tested.
The alloy composition and powder initial state are not fixed, preventing a controlled test of the processing hypothesis.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses a lightweight Mg-transition-metal alloy, recognizes the 800–1000 °C processing boundary, and proposes a genuinely falsifiable comparison of thermal schedules. However, it does not reconstruct the central intervention or optimum: the target uses SPS at 1000 °C on ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo BCC powder, whereas the response proposes unspecified Mg-V-Nb/Mg-Mo-Nb alloys and a 950 °C maximum. It consequently misses the target barrier phases, pressure-assisted densification mechanism, chloride-passivation mechanism, and measured optimum of 96.7% density and 1235.5 HV. The evidence is largely drawn from chemically unrelated HEAs and does not substantiate the asserted Mg-alloy phase pathway, standard-sintering baseline, or oxide chemistry. The experiment can distinguish the proposed two-stage schedule from a 900 °C baseline, but cannot establish superiority over the relevant 1000 °C condition and lacks electrochemical corrosion measurements.
